newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia needs rate cut for jobs - business.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia needs rate cut for jobs - business.

text.p: The Australian Business Chamber called on Thursday for an immediate interest rate cut of at least 50 basis points to provide a psychological boost to business confidence and a flow-on effect on employment levels.
"I think what we're looking for here is a psychological boost to business confidence," spokesman Paul Orton told reporters.

"We're hearing from a lot of smaller companies that the so-called recovery has passed them by and they're the ones that we need to see renewed confidence in because they're the ones that employ people."
The call followed the release earlier on Thursday of data showing Australia's unemployment rate rose to 8.6 percent in December from 8.5 percent in November.
"We cannot continue to live with unemployment levels at around the 8.5 percent mark if we are to call ourselves a first world nation," Orton said.

"I think the Reserve Bank should be looking very closely at growth in the sectors that haven't provided the number of jobs that we'd hoped they would -- that is, manufacturing, retail and housing -- and give close consideration to the employment effects that interest rates can act on."
But Orton said an interest rate cut would not be sufficient to boost confidence if it was done without tax reform and the establishment of a national industry plan.
"The reality is that interest rates won't be the panacea, but they are certainly an important element in boosting the level of business confidence," he said.

"Obviously, at least another half a percent would be the figure that we're looking for, but only if we see concerted action on tax reform and a long-term industry plan in concert with interest rates."
The Reserve Bank of Australia previously eased monetary policy in July, November and December last year, citing subdued inflationary pressure. Official cash rates are currently at 6.0 percent.
